_note: Box metadata only. The box wording itself is read verbatim from QSS Ch1-4.pdf at runtime (pdfbox.js + box_geom.json). blanks: preferred key terms to blank out when they appear in a sentence. wrong: deliberately false statements used as the answer in 'which is FALSE' questions.

wrong: Experimental research examines how an outcome is correlated with a treatment without manipulating anything.
It assigns the same value of the treatment variable to every observation.
It then measures each observation's pretreatment covariates only.
For each observation i, the causal effect of a binary treatment Ti is the difference between the treated group's mean and the control group's mean.
Yi(1) is the outcome observed for unit i before treatment is assigned.
Yi(0) is the average outcome of all control units.
We observe both potential outcomes, but only for units in the treatment group.
Which potential outcome is observed is chosen by the researcher after the study.
Formally, the observed outcome Yi equals Yi(1) − Yi(0).
The SATE is the difference in average outcomes between the treated and control groups in the sample.
Its formula is SATE = (1/n1) Σ_{i=1}^{n} Ti {Yi(1) − Yi(0)} (equation 2.1).
n is the number of treated units.
Σ_{i=1}^{n} multiplies the terms together from i = 1 to i = n.
In an RCT, each unit chooses whether to join the treatment group or the control group.
Randomization guarantees that every individual's causal effect can be observed directly.
This is because the two groups are exactly identical in every observed characteristic in any single sample.
The main advantage of RCTs is their improved external validity.
Internal validity is the extent to which the study's conclusions generalize beyond the study.
One weakness of RCTs is a potential lack of internal validity.
External validity is the extent to which the causal assumptions hold within the study sample.
The Hawthorne effect is when study subjects behave differently because they were randomly assigned to the control group.
A confounder is a posttreatment variable affected by the treatment.

blanks: both the treatment and the outcome
wrong: A confounder is associated with the outcome but not with the treatment.
A confounder reduces bias in the estimation of the treatment effect.
Confounding bias can be eliminated entirely through statistical control.
One example is subclassification: comparing treated and control units that have different values of a confounding variable.
The before-and-after design compares treated and control units after treatment only.
It adjusts for any confounding factor that changes over time.
It fully addresses bias due to time-varying confounders.
The DiD design estimates the sample average treatment effect (SATE) for all units.
The DiD estimate is (Ȳtreated,after − Ȳcontrol,after) − (Ȳtreated,before + Ȳcontrol,before).
The first difference is the difference for the control group; the second is for the treatment group.
It assumes the treatment and control groups have identical outcome levels before treatment.
If n is odd, the median is the average of x_(n/2) and x_(n/2+1).
If n is even, the median is x_(n/2), the lower of the two middle observations.
x_(i) denotes the i-th observation in the order it appears in the data.
The median is more sensitive to outliers than the mean, so it is a less robust measure of center.
Quantiles are data values that divide the range of the variable into equal-width intervals.
Quartiles divide the observations into 25 groups; percentiles into 100 groups.
The 25th percentile is the median, and the 75th percentile is the maximum.
The interquartile range is the difference between the maximum and minimum, and it measures the center of a distribution.
The sample standard deviation measures the average value of the data.
It is defined as (1/n) Σ_{i=1}^{n} |xi − x̄|, the mean absolute deviation.
x̄ is the sample median.
About half of the data points lie more than 2 standard deviations away from the mean.
The square root of the standard deviation is called the variance.
A histogram divides the data into bins, where the height of each bin represents the proportion of observations that fall within it.

blanks: divided by the width of the bin
wrong: The height of each bin represents density: the number of observations in the bin multiplied by the width of the bin.
A histogram shows the relationship between two variables.
A box plot visualizes a distribution by indicating its mean and standard deviation.
It also indicates the points more than 3 standard deviations from the mean.
It shows the full shape of a single distribution better than a histogram.

boxes.term: Simple random sampling, probability sampling, sample selection bias

wrong: Simple random sampling (SRS) is a form of quota sampling.
SRS avoids sample selection bias by choosing units that match the population on known demographics.
Under SRS, units are selected with replacement, each with a probability proportional to its size.
The resulting sample is representative of the population only in terms of observed characteristics.
The natural log transformation is often used to make negative values positive.

blanks: extremely large or small positive values
wrong: These are variables with many negative values.
The natural logarithm is the logarithm with base 10, defined as y = log_10 x.
It is the inverse of the square function, so x = y².
There are two types of nonresponse in survey research: sampling nonresponse and frame nonresponse.
Unit nonresponse is when a respondent skips a particular question.
Item nonresponse is when a sampled person cannot be contacted at all.
Both always bias inferences, regardless of who responds.
A scatter plot graphically compares the distributions of one variable across two groups.
It plots the quantiles of one variable against the quantiles of the other.
The Gini coefficient measures the average income in a society.

blanks: one person possesses all the wealth
wrong: It ranges from −1, when everyone has the same wealth, to 1, when one person possesses all the wealth.
The z-score of the i-th observation measures its percentile rank in the data.
It is defined as (xi − Sx) / x̄, where x̄ and Sx are the mean and standard deviation of x.
The z-score changes whenever the variable is rescaled, for example from dollars to thousands of dollars.
Correlation measures the degree to which one variable causes another.
It is defined as the average of the differences between the z-scores of x and y.
x̄ and ȳ are the medians, and Sx and Sy are the ranges, of x and y.
Correlation ranges from 0 to 1.
It doubles when one of the variables is measured in units twice as large.
A Q-Q plot plots each observation's value of one variable against its value of another variable.
If the two distributions are identical, all points lie on a horizontal line.
If the points form a line steeper than 45 degrees, the distribution on the horizontal axis is more dispersed.
If the slope is less than 45 degrees, the distribution on the vertical axis has a larger mean.
The k-means algorithm chooses the number of clusters automatically from the data.
Step 1: assign every observation to the same cluster.
Step 2: assign each observation to the cluster whose centroid is farthest away.
Step 3: choose the new centroid of each cluster as the within-cluster median observation.
Step 4: repeat Step 1 with new random centroids until k clusters are found.
Prediction error = predicted outcome − actual outcome, squared.
The average squared prediction error is called bias; a prediction is unbiased when its bias is one.
The root mean square of prediction error represents the direction of the average prediction error.
Classification is the problem of predicting a continuous outcome.
A classification is judged by its RMSE.
In binary classification there is only one type of misclassification.
A false positive is a correctly predicted negative outcome.
The correlation coefficient quantifies any relationship between two variables, linear or not.
An upward trend in a scatter plot's data cloud implies a negative correlation.
Correlation is the best measure for a quadratic relationship.
The linear regression model is Y = αX + β + ε.
X is the outcome variable and Y is the predictor.
ε is the residual, which is directly observed in the data.
The slope β represents the average outcome when the predictor equals zero.
With estimates (α̂, β̂), we predict the outcome at X = x as Ŷ = α̂x + β̂.
The residual is ε̂ = Ŷ − Ȳ, the fitted value minus the mean.
A common method for estimating the coefficients is to maximize the correlation between X and the residuals.
Least squares minimizes the sum of the residuals, Σ ε̂i.
The mean of the residuals equals the mean of Y.
The regression line always goes through the origin (0, 0).
The estimated slope equals the ρ-unit increase in the outcome associated with a one-unit increase in the predictor.
Here ρ is the coefficient of determination.
Regression towards the mean is a causal effect of the predictor.
An observation whose predictor value is farther from the mean tends to have an outcome even farther from the mean.
This tendency can only be explained by a real change in the units over time.
The coefficient of determination (R²) is a measure of causal effect size.
It represents the proportion of observations predicted exactly by the model.
It is defined as the ratio of the total sum of squares (TSS) to the sum of squared residuals (SSR).
With experimental data and a single binary treatment, the estimated intercept is the average treatment effect.
That slope is always smaller than the difference-in-means estimator.
The estimated intercept equals the estimated average outcome under the treatment condition.
The linear model's functional form alone permits this causal interpretation, even without randomization.
The multiple regression model is Y = α × X1 × X2 × ... × Xp + ε.
βj is the increase in the average outcome associated with a one-unit increase in Xj, letting the other variables change freely.

blanks: minimizing the sum of squared residuals
wrong: The coefficients are estimated by fitting a separate simple regression for each predictor.
No adjustment is needed to R² when predictors are added.
An example of a model with an interaction term is Y = α + β1X1 + β2X2 + ε.
The model assumes that the effect of X1 is the same at every value of X2.
As X2 increases by one unit, the average outcome goes up by β3 regardless of X1.
The regression discontinuity design is a method for analyzing randomized experiments only.
RD assumes that treated and control units are comparable at every value of the forcing variable.
RD often has weak internal validity.

blanks: away from the point of discontinuity
wrong: RD has strong external validity because it uses the whole range of the forcing variable.
